Let’s reason through this.  

Amphibians rely on lungs but also use skin and buccal respiration — they still need supplementary gas exchange, especially in aquatic stages or as adults in some species.  
Reptiles have better-developed lungs than amphibians and generally do not rely on skin or gills for gas exchange as adults, so they can meet respiratory needs with lungs alone.  
Mammals also have adequate lung tissue, but they evolved after reptiles, so reptiles were the first group to achieve this.  
Trematoda are flatworms, which do not have lungs at all.  

Thus, reptiles were the first group to have lungs adequate without supplementary organs.  

Final answer: (B)
